text: A supplier record isn't something you create once and forget. Addresses change, sites retire, classifications expire, and sometimes the same real company ends up with two separate records. This closing lesson of Chapter 2 covers ordinary maintenance, then merging duplicates.

Most maintenance is just keeping the record current - a new address, a renewed classification, a new contact, updated payment terms after a renegotiated contract. It's the same create and edit screens from earlier lessons, used after the fact. Inactivating, not deleting, is the standard way to retire a supplier, site, or bank account - transaction history stays intact and reportable, but nothing new can post to it.

Despite registration and qualification controls, duplicates still happen - the same company entered twice under slightly different names, or an acquired supplier needing to be consolidated into the acquirer's record. Left alone, that splits purchase and payment history across two records and quietly breaks spend reporting.

A supplier merge consolidates one supplier or site into another, moving transaction references so purchase orders and invoices now point at the surviving record. You can scope it to specific sites, or just unpaid invoices. It's treated as irreversible once it completes, and Fusion won't transfer an invoice if doing so would create a duplicate invoice number on the surviving record.

Because you can't undo a merge, the discipline is reviewing both records - open invoices, unpaid balances, site assignments - before submitting it, not treating it as a quick cleanup click. That closes Chapter 2. Up next, Chapter 3: Invoices, starting with the different invoice types Payables supports.
